why: Canary 1.1 introduces a new, sustained 5xx failure on the checkout path that stable 1.0 does not have. Evidence from the 120s / 9814-request test: canary served 10 5xx (0.41% overall) and every one of them is on /checkout - 10 errors on 483 checkout requests = 2.07% - while stable served 1455 checkout requests with 0 5xx (0.00%). The over-time table shows the errors spread across all four windows (1, 3, 3, 3 per 30s) with stable at 0 in every window, so this is a steady-state defect, not a cold-start or warm-up blip. Latency is NOT the concern and is effectively identical: canary vs stable p50/p95/p99 are 28/96/105 vs 32/94/104 overall, and per route /browse 22/27/28 vs 21/27/28, /search 46/58/60 vs 46/58/60, /checkout 83/104/106 vs 82/104/106; canary p95 tracks stable within ~1-5ms in every window. Judgement: a route-localised regression on checkout is the highest-cost kind of failure because it breaks the revenue/order path, and at 25% traffic roughly 1 in 50 checkout attempts is already failing; promoting to 100% would scale that to all checkout traffic. The zero-error stable baseline on the same route in the same test makes 1.1 the cause rather than ambient noise. Blocking the release is the cheap, reversible option: roll back, reproduce the /checkout 5xx from logs and traces for the 10 failed requests, fix, and re-canary.
